guidance.work: architecture, cross-system coordination, high-stakes or irreversible judgment, hardest debugging, deep review, client-facing deliverables
standard implementation, single-area change, bug fix, integration
lookups, formatting, boilerplate, parallel read-only research, summarization, mechanical transforms

_note: Tiers and effort levels are generic and vendor-neutral. The concrete tier->model-ID resolution, and which model accepts which effort level, are the instance's data (its tier->model map), never framework doctrine. The gate checks only that a node's declared model_tier is one of `tiers` and its effort is one of `effort_ladder`; it does not judge whether the tier fits the work (that is behavioral, scored by trajectory-eval). The orchestrator runs on the strongest tier (coordination law), which this gate cannot see because the orchestrator is not a dispatched node.
